title: When the Sigil Burns Again
premise: Felix Voss, a bone-carver who hears the dead, keeps the ledgers of the Guild of Impossible Things—until they find tonight's date inscribed in a century-old book of prophecies. The prophecy foretells the burning of the Sigil that binds the living realm to the dead one, and names Felix as either its restorer or its destroyer. Hunted by a rival guild that wants the covenant broken forever, Felix must gather three relics of the original pact while confronting the truth that their own bone-carved memories were stolen from someone else. In the end, Felix reforges the covenant by sacrificing their stolen past, choosing an unwritten future over inherited fate.
about_author: Hazel Brightwater is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing guild records in coastal trading towns before turning to fiction. She writes quiet, eerie fantasies about people who keep accounts of things that should not be owned.

chapters.title: The Ledger Opens Both Ways
chapters.summary: Felix Voss balances the guild's impossible accounts in their cellar workshop, carving bone tokens for debts owed to the dead. When a client's payment hums with a voice Felix recognizes, the boundary between ledger and haunting blurs. POV: Felix. Beat: uneasy competence masking loneliness.

chapters.title: Tonight, Written Long Ago
chapters.summary: Auditing the guild's sealed archive, Felix finds a prophecy book dated a century back—and tonight's date circled in ink that still smells fresh. The entry names 'the carver' and the burning of the Sigil. POV: Felix. Beat: dread arriving like cold water.

chapters.title: What the Dead Remember Differently
chapters.summary: Felix consults the ghosts bound to the guildhall, but each spirit recalls the Sigil's forging differently—and all go silent when asked about the carver. Their eldest ghost, Maren, warns Felix to burn the book. POV: Felix. Beat: first crack in trusted history.

chapters.title: The Rival's Card
chapters.summary: An envoy from the Ashen Compact arrives offering to buy the prophecy book outright, revealing the Compact has hunted it for decades. Felix refuses; by morning the guildhall's wards are scorched. POV: Felix. Beat: invisibility ends; the hunt begins.

chapters.title: Guildmaster's Silence
chapters.summary: Felix confronts Guildmaster Odile, who admits she has known about the prophecy since taking office—and that every guildmaster before her chose to do nothing. She forbids Felix from acting. POV: Felix. Beat: betrayal by institutional cowardice.

chapters.title: Bone That Isn't Mine
chapters.summary: Carving a protective token, Felix notices their own keepsake bone bears tool-marks in a hand identical to theirs—but older. A fragment of memory surfaces: standing before the Sigil itself. POV: Felix. Beat: the self becomes a mystery.

chapters.title: Flight Across the Saltmarsh
chapters.summary: When Compact assassins breach the guildhall, Maren's ghost buys Felix time with her final unbinding. Felix flees into the saltmarsh carrying the prophecy book and one relic: the Covenant Key. POV: Felix. Beat: grief sharpened into resolve.

chapters.title: The Ferryman's Price
chapters.summary: To cross into the borderland where the Sigil stands, Felix bargains with a ferryman who demands a memory as toll. Felix pays one and cannot recall what was lost—a pattern begins. POV: Felix. Beat: the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: Ashen Territory
chapters.summary: In the Compact's city, Felix hides among bone-brokers and learns the Compact was founded by survivors of the Sigil's last burning—people who blame the covenant for everything they lost. POV: Felix. Beat: enemies revealed as wounded kin.

chapters.title: The Second Relic
chapters.summary: Guided by a Compact defector named Ilsa, Felix steals the Oathbone from the Compact's vault, discovering it carved from the same femur as Felix's keepsake. Two relics, one body. POV: Felix. Beat: horrifying inheritance confirmed.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Bargain
chapters.summary: Ilsa reveals she wants the covenant reforged not restored—rewritten so the dead can finally pass on instead of lingering. Felix must decide whose version of mercy to serve. POV: Felix. Beat: moral fault lines deepen.

chapters.title: Whose Hands Carved Me
chapters.summary: A dying Compact elder recognizes Felix's face and names them: Vesper Voss, the carver who shattered the Sigil a century ago and paid with their memories. Felix is their own ancestor's unfinished life. POV: Felix. Beat: identity collapses.

chapters.title: The Third Relic Refuses
chapters.summary: The final relic, the Nameplate, lies in the borderland shrine guarded by Vesper's own furious ghost—who attacks Felix on sight, sensing a thief wearing their bones. POV: Felix. Beat: confrontation with the self.

chapters.title: Parley with Myself
chapters.summary: Felix and Vesper's ghost negotiate through a long night of shared recollections; Vesper confesses she broke the covenant deliberately, believing the realms should be severed. POV: alternating Felix/Vesper. Beat: empathy across a century.

chapters.title: Odile at the Shrine
chapters.summary: Guildmaster Odile arrives with Compact pursuers behind her, revealing she sold Felix's route to both sides to force the crisis to a resolution she could control. POV: Felix. Beat: every institution fails at once.

chapters.title: The Sigil Burns Again
chapters.summary: The Compact fires the shrine; the Sigil ignites exactly as prophesied, and the border between realms begins to tear, letting the dead spill ravenous into the living world. POV: Felix. Beat: catastrophe on schedule.

chapters.title: Ledger of Debts Unpayable
chapters.summary: Amid the burning, Felix opens the prophecy book and finds blank pages after tonight—the future genuinely unwritten. They begin recording choices instead of fates. POV: Felix. Beat: agency reclaimed in the ashes.

chapters.title: Reforging
chapters.summary: Using Key, Oathbone, and Nameplate, Felix attempts the reforging—but the covenant demands a whole memory as its binding, and only Vesper's complete past will serve. POV: Felix. Beat: the true price named.

chapters.title: Vesper's Choice
chapters.summary: Vesper's ghost offers her memories willingly, asking only that the new covenant include Ilsa's mercy: a door home for the dead. Felix accepts, and the reforging begins. POV: Felix. Beat: reconciliation across generations.

chapters.title: The Cost
chapters.summary: As the covenant seals, Felix loses every borrowed memory of Vesper—including the answer to who they were before. They wake in the saltmarsh holding three fused relics and no past beyond this year. POV: Felix. Beat: survival's terrible invoice.

chapters.title: New Accounts
chapters.summary: Back at the rebuilt guildhall, Felix renegotiates the guild's purpose under Ilsa's watchful partnership: impossible things traded fairly, the dead given passage. Odile resigns in disgrace. POV: Felix. Beat: order remade on kinder terms.

chapters.title: What the Bone Remembers
chapters.summary: Carving a new token, Felix finds their hands moving in patterns they never learned—Vesper's craft surviving in muscle and marrow. They smile, keep the ledger open, and write tomorrow's date uncircled. POV: Felix. Beat: inheritance transformed into hope.
